Steps for beginning your doctorate
Doctoral guidelines Step 5: Enrollment
Enrollment is now legally mandatory for all doctoral researchers in Baden-Württemberg. Within the same semester you have been admitted to your faculty as a doctoral researcher, you must go through the two-step process of admission and enrollment at the university. You are required to remain enrolled at the university throughout your entire doctoral training until you have completed your thesis defense.
It is possible to enroll at any time during the year although we recommend that enrollment take place before the end of the re-registration period:
June 15 to July 15 for the winter semester
January 15 to February 15 for the summer semester
Admission to the University
Whether you have received the letter of admission (Annahme als Doktorand) from your faculty, or you are waiting for it, you must apply for admission to the university. These are the important dates to keep in mind:
Applications for the summer semester can be submitted beginning on January 15. (The summer semester runs from April 1 through September 30.)
Applications for the winter semester can be submitted beginning on June 15. (The winter semester runs from October 1 through March 31.)
Links
If you have received the letter of admission from your faculty, you may apply for admission to the university.
Application as a regular doctoral researcher
Do you already have your admission letter from the faculty (Annahme als Doktorand)? Complete your formal university application as a regular doctoral researcher here. Get step‑by‑step guidance on document preparation, heiCO registration, and the final steps to secure your official enrollment.
If you have not yet received the letter of admission from your faculty, you may apply and enroll with the status predoc
Application for temporary enrollment
Haven’t received your letter of admission from your faculty (Annahme als Doktorand) yet? Apply for temporary erollment as predoc ("in preparation for doctoral training”, in German "Vorbereitung für die Promotion") while finalizing preparations. Find clear guidance on deadlines, health insurance registration, required documents, and the online heiCO application process for a smooth transition into your doctoral training.
Enrolling at the University
After you have completed the procedure of admission and received the admission notification from the University in your heiCO account, you can proceed with the enrollment in heiCO.
Links
Online Enrollment Procedure for Regular Doctoral Researchers at Heidelberg University
Enrollment procedure as a regular doctoral researcher
Complete your enrollment in heiCO after faculty admission. Follow the step‑by‑step guide to accept your study offer, upload certified documents, pay fees, and secure official doctoral status at Heidelberg University.
Online Enrollment Procedure for Temporary Enrollment as predoc
Enrollment procedure for temporary enrollment
Complete your temporary enrollment entirely via heiCO. Upload signed forms, certified academic records, and settle semester fees. Register with the public health insurance database within three months of the semester start. Includes specific guidelines for Italian degree verification and Chinese notarization requirements.
Fees and re-registration
Contributions and Fees
Semester fees
Enrollment is obligatory for doctoral candidates. Doctoral candidates are not required to pay tuition fees. However, in order to enroll, you will have to pay a semester fee. Please be aware that regardless of when you enroll during the semester, you will be required to pay the full semester fee for that semester. This is true even if you enroll late in the semester. Partial payments of the semester fee are not possible.
Management of Studies
Re-registration
In order to remain enrolled at the University, you must re-register each semester by paying the fee described above. The time periods for re-registration are as follows:
- June 15 to July 15 for the winter semester (October 1 to March 31),
- January 15 to February 15 for the summer semester (April 1 to September 30).
If you have any questions about the amount shown or other questions about re-registration, please contact us by e-mail at rueckmeldung@uni-heidelberg.de. Please state your full name and matriculation number as well as the key word “re-registration” in the subject line.
Advantages of enrollment
Access to services provided by the student services organisation Studierendenwerk, such as housing in the student dormitories, the multifunctional student ID card, child care services, legal and psychological counselling etc.,
Complete accident insurance coverage (for more information about insurance see our website Insurance for International Doctoral Researchers).
Studierendenwerk Heidelberg
Insurance for International Doctoral Researchers
Exemption from mandatory enrollment
Doctoral researchers admitted to their faculties before April 1, 2018 are not obligated to enroll. These doctoral researchers can choose whether or not they wish to enroll.
Doctoral researchers who have an employment contract of 50% or more of the regular working hours with Heidelberg University, the Heidelberg University Hospital or the University Medical Center Mannheim can apply to be exempted from mandatory enrollment. Doctoral researchers who wish to exempt themselves should apply by sending this form to the Zentrales Doktorandenbüro. For information about applying for exemption from mandatory enrollment, please contact them at
zdb@uni-heidelberg.de
Application form for exemption from mandatory enrollment
Previous steps
Step 3
Registration in heiDOCS
Applying for admission to the faculty needs to start as early as possible at the beginning of your doctoral training. You must begin the procedure by creating your own heiDOCS Online Doctoral File which will accompany you until the completion of your doctoral journey.
Step 4
Admission to the faculty
Once your first registration in heiDOCS is completed, you will be required to submit further documents to the doctoral office at your faculty. Review the specific document checklist—including degree proofs, exposé, and supervisor letter—and learn about validity periods and extension rules for both individual and structured programs.
